notes: San Francisco Bay Guardian, 27 October 1966 to the end of 1976, the first 173 issues in the Internet Archive collection, read from its DjVu text. Hand-curated: article passages and event-word clusters were read and each finding's quote checked against the issue. People rule as in the dossier: no owners, staff, tenants, performers or customers.

coverage.remaining: 823 issues, 1977 to 2014: next 1977–1986 (153 issues), then 1988–1994 (179), 1998–2006 (122) and 2008–2014 (395, lower value: those years were on the open web).
coverage.note: 173 issues; 25,304 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, of which the advertisement filter marked 19,662 and kept 1,835 windows (639 rescued for an event word) in 1,264 address clusters. The paper's numbered addresses are overwhelmingly display advertisements and calendar listings, so the clusters were filtered three ways and each result read: 134 clusters of article prose (all read), 224 event-word clusters under the tighter filter (the first 193 lines of 671 read, nearly all advertisements, then stopped) and 23 event-word passages (all read). About 100 candidates were checked against the issue text; 52 were written and 4 dropped at the overlap check as already on their pages (Bechtel's 50 Beale, Toad Hall's 1973 fire, the Daughters of Bilitis at 1005 Market, Small Press Traffic at 558 Castro). 48 findings, each quote found again in the issue's text. 37 resolved and published on 35 pages, none seeded; 1 of them placed by hand (1823 Sutter, inside the parcel 1821–1825). 4 held as single facts on parcels with no page (3220 Fillmore, 2695 Sacramento, 2140 Clement, 2260 Van Ness). 7 unresolved at numbers EAS no longer holds or cannot join to one parcel: 1330 Clay, 17 Second, 432 Mason, 17 Adler Place, 75 Fifth, 1898 Folsom and 393 Folsom. The audit flags 2 of 48, both a building the article names without a number: the Western Merchandise Mart (1355 Market) and the Gartland Apartments (the corner of 16th and Valencia); each placement note says so. Not yet done: an advertisement-unfiltered pass for list-style articles such as the nursing-home inspection list of 13 December 1972, of which one entry was taken.

findings.description: In 1973 the Press Club of San Francisco at 555 Post Street had 2,952 members, of whom its president said only 187 were newsmen; it was then being sued for discriminating against women.

raw.text: beat a track to 555 Post Street
